title: Eventual vanishing of a module map on one affine open
statement: Let I be a directed preorder and R:I\to\mathrm{CRing} a diagram. Let c be a limiting cone of the inverse diagram of spectra with affine vertex S. Fix i\le j in I and any scheme morphism f:X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i) [def-pc-scheme]. Write X_k=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}\operatorname{Spec}(R_k) and X=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}S, with projections p_k:X_k\to X_i [def-pc-base-change]. Let F,G be quasi-coherent modules on X_j, F of finite type and G of finite presentation [pqf-def-coherent], and let \delta:F\to G have zero tensor pullback to X. For any affine open U\subseteq X_i, there is l\ge j such that, for every k\ge l and every open W\subseteq p_k^{-1}(U), the map on W-sections of the tensor pullback of \delta to X_k is zero. There is no quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or finite-presentation hypothesis on f.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (3), first proof; Algebra Tag 05N7 (3), finite-generator vanishing argument

proof.text: Restrict the fixed models to the inverse image of the chosen affine open U of X_i. All later inverse images and the limit inverse image are affine, since the maps between the base spectra are affine. By the affine finite type criterion the source has finitely generated sections, and the target has finitely presented sections. The affine pullback-sections comparison identifies the maps with scalar extensions, naturally in the module morphism.

The coordinate rings of these affine inverse images form a directed colimit: Spec carries the colimit of the base rings to the given limit, the upper tail is cofinal, and tensor product with the coordinate ring of U commutes with colimits. Choose finite generators for the source. Present the target by a finite matrix P. Lift the image of each generator to a finite free vector. Its image at the limit is in the image of P. Represent the finitely many coefficients of the witnesses at one stage; then the finitely many entries of the resulting difference vectors are zero at a later common stage by the elementwise filtered-colimit equality criterion. Every generator consequently has zero image.

The corresponding module homomorphism is zero, so its associated sheaf map is zero on every subopen. Further scalar extension preserves zero. The composition comparison for tensor pullback identifies further pullback with the direct pullback from the original stage. This gives the asserted vanishing on every subopen at every stage above the one chosen. Empty affines and zero modules are included.
